transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I’ve been having a hard time staying with things at work. Like, I’ll start a safety briefing or go over a plan trying to pay attention, and a few minutes in my head’s already on three other job problems. Then I miss stuff I really should’ve caught.
Did you have trouble paying attention like this when you were a child?

Yeah. I mean, from pretty early on, like elementary school. Teachers would tell my parents I couldn’t stay in my seat, I’d talk when I wasn’t supposed to, lose homework… stuff like that. I guess I’d also rush through directions before I really understood what they wanted.
Have you ever had a period when your mood was unusually high or unusually irritable for several days in a row?
I don’t think so. I mean, I get irritated like anyone, but not some several-day thing where my mood was really high or out of character.
Do these attention problems also cause trouble for you outside of work, like at home or in daily life?

Yeah… it does. At home, my wife’s pretty tired of having to remind me about things I said I’d take care of. And at work it’s gotten noticed too — missed follow-ups, site coordination getting messy. My employer’s brought it up formally, so… it’s not just me being a little scattered.

latest_inference.note: Lifelong inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity since childhood with impairment in multiple settings strongly supports ADHD; symptoms are not limited to a stressor and there is no evidence here for anxiety, depressive, or trauma/stressor disorder. Prior questioning also reduced concern for bipolar-spectrum causes.
